newsitem.title: USA: National carlot beef trade weekly review - USDA.
newsitem.headline: National carlot beef trade weekly review - USDA.

text.p: Boxed beef trading started the week with very slow demand and generally steady price levels, but offerings were moderate to heavy, USDA said.
These conditions continued to midweek, with both the retail and HRI interest for immediate needs, and demand was light at the previous week's price levels.

Chuck and round cuts were the first to show weakness and by the end of the trading period these cuts were trading at lower price levels, mainly to control inventories on these items. Select cuts showed the most weakness by the end of the trading period and traded at the lower price levels.

However, loin cuts continued to trade at higher price levels most of the week on both the Choice and Select cuts. The rib cuts showed weakness as the week progressed with demand for these cuts very slow.
Closely trimmed items were under somewhat the same pressure and traded lower on most items, again the Select cuts were under the most pressure during the trading week.
Beef trimmings were weak on rather light demand and light to moderate offerings. Fed cattle and blended coarse ground items traded higher on light-moderate demand, light offerings.

For the week - Select and Choice rib primal steady to 2.00 lower; Select and Choice chuck primal 4.00 to 5.00 lower; Select and Choice round primal 1.50 to 3.00 lower; Select and Choice loin primal 2.00 to 5.00 higher; Closely trimmed items 1.00 to 1.50 lower; Beef trimmings 1.00 lower; Fed cattle and blended coarse ground items 3.00 to 7.00 higher.

The Estimated Composite of Boxed Beef Cutout values of Choice 1-3 550/700 carcasses Dn .55 at 106.70; 700/850 Dn .64 at 106.54; Select 1-3 550/700 carcasses Dn 1.34 at 102.49; 700/850 Dn 1.42 at 102.04.

COW AND BULL CARCASS, BONELESS PROCESSING BEEF, CUTTER COW CUTOUT The boneless beef market continued to see sharp price advances throughout the trading period on moderate demand and light offerings. Limited available supplies, brought on by continued reduced marketings of slaughter cows, fueled the advance. Buyers were forced to pay higher asking prices but began to look for alternative grinding materials and cut back on their overall needs.

Cow carcasses moved higher on limited offerings as most slaughters had barely enough production for their own grinding needs. Cow cuts moved sharply higher as well, driven by the same shortage of slaughter cows.

Price advances were noted on all cuts. Utility carcasses 6.00-7.00 higher; Cutter 5.00-6.00 higher; 90% boneless beef 8.00-10.00 higher; 85% mostly 8.00 higher; 75% 4.50 higher; 65% mostly 6.00 higher. The Cutter cow carcass gross cut-out value for Thursday, March 06, 1997 was estimated at 86.28 per cwt., up 7.80 from a week ago Friday.
